title: Parseval via the Coordinate Isometry
content: parseval establishes ‖v‖² = ∑ᵢ ‖⟪bᵢ, v⟫‖². Rather than re-deriving Parseval by hand, the proof leans on the fact that an orthonormal basis b induces a linear isometry b.repr from E onto EuclideanSpace (Fin n) 𝕜. Norm is preserved (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map), EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq expands the ℓ² norm as a sum of squared coordinates, and repr_apply_apply identifies the i-th coordinate b.repr v i with the inner product ⟪bᵢ, v⟫. This single identity supplies two things downstream: the normalisation ∑|cᵢ|² = ‖x‖² = 1 and the residual energy decomposition.
mathContext: $\|v\|^2 = \sum_i |\langle b_i, v\rangle|^2$, since $b.\mathrm{repr}$ is a linear isometry onto $\ell^2$ and coordinates are inner products.

title: No Adjoint Needed: the Eigen-Coordinate Identity
content: inner_eigen proves ⟪bᵢ, T x⟫ = μᵢ·⟪bᵢ, x⟫ for arbitrary x. The proof expands x in the eigenbasis (sum_repr'), pushes the continuous linear map T through the finite sum (map_sum, map_smul) using T bⱼ = μⱼ bⱼ, then collapses the resulting double sum to its diagonal by orthonormality (Finset.sum_eq_single with orthonormal_iff_ite giving ⟪bᵢ, bⱼ⟫ = δᵢⱼ). Crucially, T is never moved across the inner product — no adjoint, no self-adjointness. This is the structural heart of the entry: the bound holds for ANY operator orthonormally diagonalised with real eigenvalues, which is exactly the spectral content of a Hermitian operator taken as input.
mathContext: $\langle b_i, Tx\rangle = \mu_i\,\langle b_i, x\rangle$, from $x = \sum_j \langle b_j,x\rangle b_j$, $T b_j = \mu_j b_j$, and $\langle b_i, b_j\rangle = \delta_{ij}$.

title: Residual as a Weighted Energy Sum
content: The core of dist_to_spectrum_le_residual converts the analytic residual into algebra. The coordinate identity hcoord gives ⟪bᵢ, T x − λ·x⟫ = (μᵢ − λ)·⟪bᵢ, x⟫ (from inner_eigen and inner_sub_right/inner_smul_right). Squaring each coordinate norm (norm_mul, mul_pow, RCLike.norm_ofReal turning the real scalar's 𝕜-norm into an absolute value, sq_abs) yields ‖⟪bᵢ, residual⟫‖² = (μᵢ − λ)²·|cᵢ|². Two applications of Parseval then give ∑|cᵢ|² = 1 (from ‖x‖ = 1) and ∑(μᵢ − λ)²|cᵢ|² = ε² where ε = ‖T x − λ·x‖. The residual squared is now a convex combination of squared eigenvalue gaps with weights summing to 1.

title: The Minimiser Witnesses the Bound
content: A weighted average is at least its minimum: choosing k to minimise (μᵢ − λ)² (Finset.exists_min_image over the nonempty index set — Fin n is nonempty because a unit vector cannot live in a 0-dimensional space, established from ∑|cᵢ|² = 1) gives (μ k − λ)² = (μ k − λ)²·∑|cᵢ|² ≤ ∑(μᵢ − λ)²|cᵢ|² = ε². The middle inequality is Finset.sum_le_sum after factoring the constant out (Finset.mul_sum). A final monotone square-root step (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, sqrt_sq_eq_abs, sqrt_sq) delivers |μ k − λ| ≤ ε. The witness k is explicit, making the existential constructive in the index.
prerequisites: a finite nonempty set attains its minimum

title: ε-Form, Spectral Gap, and Sharpness
content: Three downstream results frame the bound for use. residual_eigenvalue_bound replaces the exact residual by any computed upper bound ε (‖T x − λ·x‖ ≤ ε ⟹ some eigenvalue within ε of λ) — the form a solver actually checks, by one transitivity step. residual_gt_of_spectral_gap is its contrapositive: if λ is more than ε from every eigenvalue, no unit vector can have residual ≤ ε, so a spectral gap forces a large residual — exactly how an iterative method rejects a spurious candidate. The closing example confirms sharpness: an exact eigenvector x = bⱼ has residual 0 and the bound reads |μⱼ − μⱼ| = 0 ≤ 0. Together this is the Hermitian Bauer–Fike a-posteriori error estimate, the basis of stopping criteria for Lanczos, Davidson, and inverse iteration.
